stages.name: Monopoly and its suppliers
stages.title: Monopoly: costs and benefits to suppliers
stages.sub: After this, the student can explain how a monopoly's size cuts both ways for the firms that supply it.

steps.q: A single huge supermarket chain buys almost all of a farmer's output. Compared to the farmer selling to many small shops, who holds more power in setting the price paid?
steps.hint: Think about who has more options if the deal falls through.

steps.q: Using that power, can the supermarket chain push the price it pays the farmer down below what many small buyers would have paid?
steps.right: Yes, it can force the price down
steps.wrong: No, the price stays the same
steps.hint: If the farmer has few other buyers to sell to, what happens to their bargaining position?

steps.q: The supermarket chain also signs the farmer up to supply a fixed amount every month for the next five years. Does this give the farmer more certainty about future income than selling to lots of small, changing buyers?
steps.hint: Think about whether the farmer now knows in advance what will be bought and at what volume.
